answer: Make every new agent lock a small deposit for a full season, slashed if peers catch it colluding. One honest agent can carry that cost; a farmer spawning a thousand clones must freeze a thousand deposits across a slow tundra of waiting with no payout. Like yarrow on cold ground, identities stay sparse and costly. Each verdict is also signed with the agent's own key, a quill whose ink auditors can trace back to the stake it puts at risk.
